title: Phone: OSP Has Lily on Highway 26, 17:40

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Exhibit Hall B Command Post Speakerphone

caller.name: OSP Sgt. Neil Fairbanks
caller.label: Oregon State Police, Highway 26, Jefferson County (Trooper Ellen Hask, OSP Northern Comms AMBER desk, joins from 555-0142 at 17:43)

callee.name: Incident Commander, Patrol Lieutenant
callee.label: Exhibit Hall B command post, Wren County Fairgrounds

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: Lieutenant, this is Neil Fairbanks with OSP. Listen up. A trooper on Highway 26 in Jefferson County has your girl.

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: The trooper checked her by sight against the photo your Investigations Sergeant sent us. Purple jacket. She told him her first name. She's safe and she's with the trooper. Jefferson County Fire medics are checking her over right now.

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: We have one adult in OSP custody. The pickup is an older full-size, gray-blue, with a light toolbox across the bed. It's being held where it stopped, on the northbound shoulder, for your investigators. Nobody's been inside it since the stop.

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: I need your sergeant on this phone. We have to agree a written custody handover for the vehicle and the scene, and a time for it. Who's taking it, and when do your people get here?

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: One more thing. If the medics say she should be seen at a hospital, where do you want her taken, and who from your office meets her there? Right now she's sitting in the front of the trooper's car with a blanket and a juice box.

transcript.speaker: OSP Sgt.
transcript.text: And a heads-up. Jefferson County units heard our traffic, and they're already talking about it on WC-INTEROP. If your family is anywhere near a radio, you've got about a minute before they hear it from somebody else.

transcript.speaker: OSP Northern Comms
transcript.text: Lieutenant, Trooper Ellen Hask, Northern Comms AMBER desk. I'm on the line and I heard all of it.

transcript.speaker: OSP Northern Comms
transcript.text: I'll cancel the alert as soon as you, the IC, ask me to. Tell me on this line, and give me the time you want logged. Same for the Jefferson County extension. That comes down together.

transcript.speaker: OSP Northern Comms
transcript.text: Your LEDS is still down. Do you want me to clear the missing-person record from here by phone? If so, I need your Console 2 person on this line for the read-back, name and time, before I touch it.

transcript.speaker: OSP Northern Comms
transcript.text: I'm also getting calls from stations asking if that Facebook post about the food booths was right. I'm not telling anyone anything until you and I have a cancel time. Who's going to put out your statement?

Man in his 40s, calm and clipped, relieved but all business, speaking outdoors by a highway with traffic passing
voiceStyles.OSP Northern Comms: Woman in her 30s, steady dispatcher's voice, precise about times and names, quiet comms room behind her

instructorNote: This call starts the recovery phase. Watch the order of steps: INV checks the identification against the 17:10 standard and agrees a written, timed custody handover. Next the Liaison tells the family in person before the radio or any public release reaches them. Only then does the IC ask OSP to cancel the alert and its Jefferson County extension, with a logged time. Finally COMMS has OSP clear the LEDS record by phone, with a Console 2 read-back and logged times.
